section.content: 为克服现有技术中锂电池的电芯强度低、电池易出现扭曲变形的技术问题，本申请提供一种水性粘结剂及改性隔膜和电池；水性粘结剂是具有核壳结构的粘结剂颗粒，所述核壳结构的粘结剂颗粒中核是聚合物A，壳是聚合物B；所述核的玻璃化转变温度为80℃～150℃；所述壳的玻璃化转变温度为30℃～70℃。本申请提供的核壳结构的粘结剂颗粒，涂覆于隔膜基材表面，制备得到的电芯经过热压后，隔膜与正负极片粘结成一体，使得电池具有更高的强度，电池的抗扭曲变形性好，同时提升隔膜的透气性，降低电池生产成本，适用于生产薄型电池，并保持好的电池性能。

In order to overcome the technical problems that the strength of a battery core of a lithium battery is low and the battery is easy to distort and deform in the prior art, the application provides the aqueous binder, the modified diaphragm and the battery; the water-based binder is binder particles with a core-shell structure, wherein the core of the binder particles with the core-shell structure is a polymer A, and the shell of the binder particles with the core-shell structure is a polymer B; the glass transition temperature of the core is 80-150 ℃; the glass transition temperature of the shell is 30-70 ℃. The application provides a binder granule of nucleocapsid structure coats in diaphragm substrate surface, and the electric core that the preparation obtained is through hot pressing after, the diaphragm bonds with positive and negative pole piece and becomes an organic whole for the battery has higher intensity, and the distortion resistance nature of battery is good, promotes the gas permeability of diaphragm simultaneously, reduces battery manufacturing cost, is applicable to the production slim battery, and keeps good battery performance.

Water-based binder, modified diaphragm, battery and preparation method of water-based binder

Technical Field

The invention belongs to the technical field of lithium battery preparation, and particularly relates to a water-based binder, a modified diaphragm, a battery and a preparation method of the water-based binder.

Background

The lithium battery has the advantages of long cycle life, wide range of service temperature, large energy density and power density, no memory effect and the like, is widely applied to 3C products such as personal computers, mobile phones and the like, and becomes the best choice of power sources of electric automobiles. With the continuous improvement of the development demand of terminal equipment, lithium batteries tend to be large-sized and thin, and on one hand, the batteries are required to have higher energy density, long cycle life and higher safety, and on the other hand, the batteries are also required to be thinner and thinner, and the batteries have certain strength. The strength of the traditional lithium battery is obviously weakened along with the thickness reduction; in particular, the battery with large area size has poor hardness, is easy to distort and deform, influences the application of devices, and even has great influence on the performance and safety of the battery. The reason for the poor strength is that the battery in the traditional battery is formed by sequentially laminating the positive electrode, the diaphragm and the negative electrode, and the electrolyte is injected into the battery, the positive electrode and the diaphragm, and the diaphragm and the negative electrode slide relatively due to the smooth surface of the diaphragm and the lubricating action after the electrolyte is added, and the positive electrode and the negative electrode are sheets which are formed by metal foils and inorganic powder and have the thickness of about hundreds of micrometers, so that the battery has insufficient strength. The battery made only depends on the physical superposition supporting strength of pole pieces about hundreds of microns, and relative displacement exists between layers, so that the battery strength cannot meet the application requirement of devices in the actual application process, and in addition, the battery has self distortion after the area of the battery is increased, the electrical property and safety of the battery are influenced, and even the battery is burnt and exploded.

In view of the above problems, the current industry adopts a solution to coat a polyolefin separator/ceramic-coated separator with an aqueous or oily PVDF polymer, and compounds a pole piece and a separator together by hot pressing to provide sufficient battery hardness and prevent distortion. Under the continuous expansion of application requirements in the fields of lithium battery manufacturing, photovoltaic back panels, energy storage and the like, PVDF shows explosive growth, and R142b serving as a main production raw material of PVDF as a fluorine chemical product can only quota production due to the fact that the atmospheric layer can be damaged and the limitation of international agreements exists, so that the risk of supply shortage exists.

Disclosure of Invention

The invention provides a water-based binder, a modified diaphragm, a battery and a preparation method of the water-based binder, aiming at the technical problems that the battery core strength of a lithium battery is low and the battery is easy to distort in the prior art.

In order to solve the technical problem, the application provides an aqueous binder, which comprises binder particles with a core-shell structure, wherein the core of the binder particles with the core-shell structure is a polymer A, and the shell of the binder particles with the core-shell structure is a polymer B;

the glass transition temperature of the core is 80-150 ℃;

the glass transition temperature of the shell is 30-70 ℃.

Preferably, the particle size of the binder particles is in the range of 1 to 10 μm; the particle size range of the core is 0.5 to 4 μm.

Preferably, the mass ratio of the core to the shell is 1: (0.2-10).

Preferably, the reactants for preparing the polymer A comprise a polymerization monomer a1, a cross-linking agent a2, a dispersing agent a3 and an initiator a4;

based on 100 percent of the mass of the polymerization reaction monomer a1, the mass proportion of the cross-linking agent a2 is 4 to 30 percent, the mass proportion of the dispersing agent a3 is 0.1 to 25 percent, and the mass proportion of the initiator a4 is 0.3 to 5 percent.

Preferably, the polymerization monomer a1 comprises one or more of acrylonitrile, methacrylonitrile, acrylates and styrene;

the cross-linking agent a2 comprises one or more of diacetone acrylamide, acetoacetoxyethyl methacrylate, N- (hydroxymethyl) acrylamide, N- (hydroxyethyl) acrylamide, divinylbenzene, diallyl phthalate and trimethylolpropane triacrylate;

the dispersant a3 comprises one or more of sodium carboxymethylcellulose (CMC), a nonionic surfactant, polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) and polyethylene glycol (PEG);

the initiator a4 comprises one or more of persulfate, azobisisobutyronitrile (AIBN), dimethyl azobisisobutyrate, dibenzoyl peroxide (BPO) and di-n-octanoyl peroxide.

Preferably, the reactants for preparing the polymer B comprise a polymerization reaction monomer B1, a cross-linking agent B2, a dispersing agent B3 and an initiator B4, and are prepared by dispersion polymerization;

based on 100 percent of the mass of the polymerization reaction monomer b1, the mass proportion of the cross-linking agent b2 is 1 to 20 percent, the mass proportion of the dispersing agent b3 is 0 to 10 percent, and the mass proportion of the initiating agent b4 is 0.5 to 5 percent.

Preferably, the polymerization monomer b1 comprises one or more of acrylonitrile, methacrylonitrile, acrylates and styrene;

the crosslinking agent b2 comprises one or more of diacetone acrylamide, acetoacetoxyethyl methacrylate, N- (hydroxymethyl) acrylamide, N- (hydroxyethyl) acrylamide, divinylbenzene, diallyl phthalate and trimethylolpropane triacrylate;

the dispersant b3 comprises one or more of sodium carboxymethylcellulose (CMC), a nonionic surfactant, polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) and polyethylene glycol (PEG);

the initiator b4 comprises one or more of persulfate, azobisisobutyronitrile (AIBN), dimethyl azobisisobutyrate, benzoyl Peroxide (BPO) and di-n-octanoyl peroxide.

In another aspect, the present application provides a method for preparing an aqueous binder, comprising the steps of:

(1) Preparation of the core solution: adding a solvent and an initiator a4 into a reaction kettle, uniformly stirring, then adding a polymerization reaction monomer a1 and a cross-linking agent a2, stirring, introducing a protective atmosphere, adding a dispersing agent a3, heating to react at the reaction temperature of 50-90 ℃ for 4-24 hours, and preparing a nuclear solution after the reaction is finished; the mass ratio of the polymerization reaction monomer a1 to the solvent is 10-45%;

(2) Preparing a core-shell structure binder: mixing the core solution with a polymer B, or mixing the core solution with a reactant for preparing the polymer B, heating to react, wherein the reaction temperature is 50-90 ℃, the reaction time is 4-24 hours, and preparing the binder with the core-shell structure after the reaction is finished;

the solvent comprises one or more of water and alcohol compounds.

On the other hand, the application provides a modified diaphragm, including coating and diaphragm substrate, the coating is for the aforesaid aqueous binder coats on diaphragm substrate surface, and the drying forms.

On the other hand, the application provides a lithium battery, including positive plate, negative pole piece and interval in adjacent positive plate and negative pole piece between the diaphragm, the diaphragm be the aforesaid modified diaphragm.

Has the advantages that:

the water-based binder comprises binder particles with a core-shell structure, wherein the glass transition temperature of a core is 80-150 ℃, and after a prepared battery cell is subjected to a hot pressing process, the core keeps the original shape, does not block a diaphragm hole, and improves the air permeability of a diaphragm; the glass transition temperature of the shell is 30-70 ℃, and the bonding force between the pole piece and the diaphragm can be improved in the hot pressing process of the battery cell prepared from the diaphragm and the pole piece; the application provides a binder granule of nucleocapsid structure coats in diaphragm substrate surface, and the electric core that the preparation obtained is through hot pressing after, the diaphragm bonds with positive and negative pole piece and becomes an organic whole for the battery has higher intensity, and the distortion resistance nature of battery is good, promotes the gas permeability of diaphragm simultaneously, reduces battery manufacturing cost, is applicable to the production slim battery, and keeps good battery performance. The water-based binder provided by the application is environment-friendly and accords with a green sustainable development road.

Detailed Description

In order to make the technical problems, technical solutions and advantageous effects solved by the present invention more clear, the present invention is further described in detail below with reference to the embodiments. It should be understood that the specific embodiments described herein are merely illustrative of the invention and are not intended to limit the invention.

The application provides an aqueous binder, which comprises binder particles with a core-shell structure, wherein the core of the binder particles with the core-shell structure is a polymer A, and the shell of the binder particles with the core-shell structure is a polymer B. The glass transition temperature of the core is 80-150 ℃, and the glass transition temperature of the shell is 30-70 ℃.

The inventor finds through a large number of experiments that the core prepared from the diaphragm and the pole piece in the lithium battery needs to be subjected to a hot pressing process, if the glass transition temperature of the core of the binder particle is lower than 80 ℃, the core is deformed and flat, and the deformed core with a certain thickness is easy to block the diaphragm hole, so that the ventilation value of the diaphragm is reduced, and the electrical property of the battery is influenced. The glass transition temperature of the core in the prepared binder particle is 80-150 ℃, the core does not deform and block the diaphragm hole after the electric core is subjected to a hot pressing process, so that the diaphragm has a high ventilation value, the ventilation property of the diaphragm is improved, and the prepared battery has good electrical property.

The application provides a binder granule of nucleocapsid structure, wherein the glass transition temperature of shell is in 30 ~ 70 ℃ within range, and the electric core that diaphragm and pole piece preparation obtained can improve the adhesion stress between pole piece and the diaphragm at the hot pressing in-process, improves the hardness of battery, and has suitable adhesion stress between the diaphragm layer of lapping diaphragm, unreels at the diaphragm and easily tears in the use, promotes the yields of diaphragm. If the glass transition temperature of the shell is lower than 30 ℃, in the preparation process of the diaphragm, the diaphragm is bonded with the diaphragm between the diaphragm layers when the diaphragm is coated and wound, the diaphragm is not easy to tear in the unwinding use process, and the yield of the diaphragm is reduced. If the glass transition temperature of the shell is higher than 70 ℃, the hardness of the shell is increased, the bonding force between the pole piece and the diaphragm is reduced in the hot pressing process of the battery core prepared from the diaphragm and the pole piece, the pole piece and the diaphragm slide relatively after liquid injection, and the hardness of the battery is reduced. The glass transition temperature of the shell is in the range of 30-70 deg.C, such as 30 deg.C, 35 deg.C, 40 deg.C, 45 deg.C, 50 deg.C, 55 deg.C, 60 deg.C, 65 deg.C, 70 deg.C, etc.

The application provides a water-based binder, including the binder granule of nuclear shell structure, wherein the glass transition temperature of nuclear is 80 ℃ -150 ℃, after the electric core that the preparation obtained is through the hot pressing process, the nuclear keeps original shape, does not block up the diaphragm hole, promotes the gas permeability of diaphragm. The glass transition temperature of the shell is 30-70 ℃, and the battery core prepared from the diaphragm and the pole piece can improve the adhesive force between the pole piece and the diaphragm in the hot pressing process. The application provides a binder particle of core-shell structure coats in diaphragm substrate surface, and the electric core that obtains of preparation is through hot pressing back, and the diaphragm bonds with positive and negative pole piece and becomes an organic whole for the battery has higher intensity, and the anti distortion nature of battery is good, promotes the gas permeability of diaphragm simultaneously, reduces battery manufacturing cost, and keeps good battery performance. The application provides a nuclear shell structure's binder granule strengthens the cohesiveness of diaphragm and pole piece, more is applicable to the production thin battery for the battery has higher intensity, also is applicable to the battery of thickness moderate or on the thick side simultaneously.

In some embodiments, the binder particles have a particle size in the range of 1 to 10 μm and the cores have a particle size in the range of 0.5 to 4 μm. Preferably, the binder particle has a particle diameter of 2 to 5 μm and the core particle has a particle diameter of 0.5 to 4 μm.

Specifically, the binder particles with the core-shell structure are mainly obtained by polymerization in a dispersion polymerization mode, and are different from the existing emulsion polymerization mode in that the size of the emulsion polymerization particles is generally not more than 1 micron, the binder particles are obtained by the dispersion polymerization mode, the particle size of the binder can be 1-10 microns, and the particle size of the core is 0.5-4 microns. The large-particle-size binder particles can increase the friction force between the diaphragm and the pole piece and improve the binding force between the diaphragm and the pole piece. For example, the particle diameter of the binder particles may be 1 μm, 2 μm, 3 μm, 4 μm, 5 μm, 6 μm, 7 μm, 8 μm, 9 μm, or 10 μm. The grain size of the core is 0.5-4 μm, and the probability of blocking the diaphragm hole can be reduced and the air permeability of the diaphragm can be improved in the coating process of the core with large grain size. The particle size of the core may be, for example, 0.5. Mu.m, 1.0. Mu.m, 1.5. Mu.m, 2.0. Mu.m, 2.5. Mu.m, 3.0. Mu.m, or 4.0. Mu.m.

In some embodiments, the mass ratio of the core to the shell is 1: (0.2-10).

In the binder particles with the core-shell structure, the core and the shell account for certain mass, and the mass ratio of the core to the shell in the binder particles with the core-shell structure provided by the application is 1: (0.2-10), the particle size of the binder particles is in the range of 1-10 microns, the particle size of the core is in the range of 0.5-4 microns, and the shell is easy to completely contain the polymer A particles inside to form a core-shell structure; the prepared binder particles are coated on the surface of the diaphragm, the diaphragm has better air permeability, the binding force between the diaphragm and the pole piece is higher, the battery has higher strength, and the high-temperature expansion rate of the battery is lower. If the mass ratio of the core to the shell is less than 1.2, namely the particle size of the shell is small, the shell cannot better coat the core, a core-shell structure cannot be formed, and sufficient peel strength cannot be provided after hot pressing. If the mass ratio of the core to the shell is higher than 1.

In some embodiments, preparing the polymer a comprises polymerizing a monomer a1, a crosslinking agent a2, a dispersant a3, and an initiator a4 by dispersion polymerization;

based on the mass of the polymerization reaction monomer a1 as 100, the mass proportion of the cross-linking agent a2 is 4-30%, the mass proportion of the dispersing agent a3 is 0.1-25%, and the mass proportion of the initiator a4 is 0.3-5%.

In some preferred embodiments, the polymerization monomer a1 comprises one or more of acrylonitrile, methacrylonitrile, acrylates, styrene; the acrylic esters comprise butyl acrylate, methyl acrylate, ethyl acrylate, methyl methacrylate, isooctyl acrylate and the like; these polymerization monomers may be used alone, or two or more of them may be used in combination, and may be selected as required. The cross-linking agent a2 comprises one or more of diacetone acrylamide, acetoacetoxyethyl methacrylate, N- (hydroxymethyl) acrylamide, N- (hydroxyethyl) acrylamide, divinylbenzene, diallyl phthalate and trimethylolpropane triacrylate; these crosslinking agents may be used alone or in combination. The dispersant a3 comprises one or more of sodium carboxymethylcellulose (CMC), a nonionic surfactant, polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) and polyethylene glycol (PEG); the nonionic surfactant can be sodium dodecyl sulfate, secondary alcohol polyoxyethylene ether surfactant Tergitol 15-S-9, secondary alcohol polyoxyethylene ether surfactant Tergitol 15-S-15, etc., and can be obtained by purchasing. The polyvinylpyrrolidone may be selected from PVP-K30, K60 or K90, and may be obtained commercially. The initiator a4 comprises one or more of persulfate, azobisisobutyronitrile (AIBN), dimethyl azobisisobutyrate, dibenzoyl peroxide (BPO) and di-n-octanoyl peroxide; the persulfate may be sodium persulfate, potassium persulfate, ammonium persulfate, or the like.

In some embodiments, preparing the polymer B comprises polymerizing the monomer B1, the crosslinking agent B2, the dispersant B3 and the initiator B4 by dispersion polymerization;

based on the mass of the polymerization reaction monomer b1 as 100, the mass of the cross-linking agent b2 is 1-20%, the mass of the dispersing agent b3 is 0-10%, and the mass of the initiator b4 is 0.5-5%.

In some preferred embodiments, the polymerization monomer b1 comprises one or more of acrylonitrile, methacrylonitrile, acrylates, styrene; the acrylic esters comprise butyl acrylate, methyl acrylate, ethyl acrylate, methyl methacrylate, isooctyl acrylate and the like; these polymerization monomers may be used alone, or two or more of them may be used in combination, and may be selected as required.

The crosslinking agent b2 comprises one or more of diacetone acrylamide, acetoacetoxyethyl methacrylate, N- (hydroxymethyl) acrylamide, N- (hydroxyethyl) acrylamide, divinylbenzene, diallyl phthalate and trimethylolpropane triacrylate; these crosslinking agents may be used alone or in combination.

The dispersant b3 comprises one or more of sodium carboxymethylcellulose (CMC), a nonionic surfactant, polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) and polyethylene glycol (PEG); the nonionic surfactant can be sodium dodecyl sulfate, secondary alcohol polyoxyethylene ether surfactant Tergitol 15-S-9, secondary alcohol polyoxyethylene ether surfactant Tergitol 15-S-15, etc., and can be obtained by purchasing.

The initiator b4 comprises one or more of persulfate, azobisisobutyronitrile (AIBN), dimethyl azobisisobutyrate, benzoyl Peroxide (BPO) and di-n-octanoyl peroxide; the persulfate may be sodium persulfate, potassium persulfate, ammonium persulfate, or the like.

In another aspect, the present application provides a method of preparing an aqueous binder, comprising the steps of:

(1) Preparation of the core solution: adding a solvent and an initiator a4 into a reaction kettle, uniformly stirring, then adding a polymerization reaction monomer a1 and a cross-linking agent a2, stirring, introducing a protective atmosphere, adding a dispersing agent a3, heating to react at the reaction temperature of 50-90 ℃ for 4-4 h, and preparing a nuclear solution after the reaction is finished; the mass ratio of the polymerization reaction monomer a1 to the solvent is 10-45%;

(2) Preparing a core-shell structure binder: mixing the core solution with a polymer B, or mixing the core solution with a reactant for preparing the polymer B, heating to react at 50-90 ℃ for 4-24 h, and preparing the core-shell structure binder after the reaction is finished;

the solvent comprises one or more of water and alcohol compounds.

The alcohol compound comprises methanol, ethanol, propanol, isobutanol, n-butanol, isopropanol, pentanol and other unit alcohols, and can also comprise propylene glycol, butanediol, glycerol and other polyhydric alcohols.

The protective atmosphere includes nitrogen and inert gases including helium, neon, argon, and the like.

Specifically, the preparation of the core-shell structure adhesive comprises two methods, namely: adding a reactant of the polymer B into the core solution, then carrying out heating reaction, and preparing the binder with the core-shell structure after the reaction is finished; the second method comprises the following steps: and firstly stirring the reactant of the polymer B, then mixing the reactant with the nuclear solution, carrying out heating reaction, and preparing the binder with the core-shell structure after the reaction is finished. The preparation steps of the first and second methods are described in detail below.

The method comprises the following steps: and adding a polymerization reaction monomer b1, a cross-linking agent b2 and a dispersing agent b3 into the core solution, uniformly stirring, adding an initiator b4, and heating for reaction to obtain the core-shell structure binder.

The second method comprises the following steps: adding solvent water, a polymerization monomer b1, a cross-linking agent b2, a dispersing agent b3 and an initiator b4 into a reaction kettle, stirring uniformly, adding the core solution, mixing uniformly, and heating for reaction to obtain the core-shell structure binder.

On the other hand, the application provides a modified diaphragm, including coating and diaphragm substrate, the coating is above-mentioned waterborne binder coats diaphragm substrate surface, and the drying forms.

Specifically, the modified diaphragm can be prepared by directly coating a water-based binder on the surface of a diaphragm substrate and drying; or the ceramic particles and the water-based binder are uniformly mixed, coated on the surface of the diaphragm base material and dried to form the diaphragm. The ceramic particles include alumina, silica, zirconia, titania, calcia, magnesia, etc., preferably alumina; or coating the water-based binder on the surface of the ceramic diaphragm substrate, and drying to form the modified diaphragm.

On the other hand, the application also provides a lithium battery, which comprises a positive plate, a negative plate and a diaphragm which is arranged between the adjacent positive plate and the negative plate at intervals, wherein the diaphragm is the modified diaphragm.

In some embodiments, the positive electrode further comprises a positive electrode current collector, and the positive electrode material layer covers the surface of the positive electrode current collector.

The positive electrode current collector comprises one or more of Al, ni, tin and copper, and preferably is selected from aluminum foil; the positive electrode active material layer further comprises a positive electrode binder and a positive electrode conductive agent, and the positive electrode active material, the positive electrode binder and the positive electrode conductive agent are blended to obtain the positive electrode material layer.

The positive active material comprises lithium cobaltate, lithium iron phosphate, lithium carbonate and the like; the binder comprises polyvinylidene fluoride, styrene butadiene rubber and a copolymer of vinylidene fluoride; the conductive agent comprises one or more of conductive carbon black, conductive carbon spheres, conductive graphite, conductive carbon fibers, carbon nanotubes, graphene or reduced graphene oxide.

The negative pole still includes the negative pole mass flow body, the negative pole material layer cover in the surface of negative pole mass flow body. The material of the negative current collector may be the same as that of the positive current collector, and thus, the description thereof is omitted. In a more preferred embodiment, the negative current collector is selected from copper foil. The negative electrode material layer comprises a negative electrode active material, and the negative electrode active material comprises graphite, hard carbon, soft carbon, graphene, mesocarbon microbeads and the like; the negative electrode material layer further comprises a negative electrode binder and a negative electrode conductive agent, and the negative electrode material layer is obtained by blending the negative electrode active material, the negative electrode binder and the negative electrode conductive agent. The negative electrode binder and the negative electrode conductive agent may be the same as the positive electrode binder and the positive electrode conductive agent, respectively, and are not described herein again.

In some embodiments, the separator substrate may be an existing conventional separator including a separator of monolayer PP (polypropylene), monolayer PE (polyethylene), bilayer PP/PE, bilayer PP/PP, and trilayer PP/PE/PP.

The present invention will be further illustrated by the following examples.

Example 1

1) Preparation of the core solution:

adding 1200g of water and 0.4g of sodium dodecyl sulfate into a glass reaction kettle, uniformly stirring, adding 300g of methyl methacrylate and 45g of divinylbenzene, stirring and introducing nitrogen for 30min, adding 1.0g of ammonium persulfate, heating to 80 ℃ for reaction, reacting for 10h, cooling to room temperature after the reaction is finished to obtain a core solution, and testing to obtain the core with the particle size of 0.75 mu m. The glass transition temperature of the test core was 125 ℃.

2) Preparing a core-shell structure binder:

adding 800g of water, 32g of sodium carboxymethylcellulose (CMC), 10g of secondary alcohol polyoxyethylene ether surfactant Tergitol 15-S-9, 200g of butyl acrylate, 467g of acrylonitrile, 20g of diallyl phthalate and 10g of AIBN into a reaction kettle, uniformly dispersing at a high speed, adding 438g of the prepared core solution, stirring at room temperature for 16h, heating to 80 ℃, and reacting at 80 ℃ for 8h to obtain a white binder with a core-shell structure, wherein the mass ratio of the core to the shell is 1: the particle size of the test binder was 1.5 μm. The glass transition temperature of the shell was measured to be 62 ℃ using DSC.

Example 2

1) Preparation of the core solution:

adding 450g of water, 450g of isopropanol, 25g of PVP-K30 and 15g of secondary alcohol polyoxyethylene ether surfactant Tergitol 15-S-15 into a glass reaction kettle, stirring uniformly, adding 300g of styrene and 30g of diallyl phthalate, stirring, introducing nitrogen for 30min, adding 10g of dibenzoyl peroxide, heating to 80 ℃, reacting for 10h at 80 ℃, cooling to room temperature after the reaction is finished to obtain a nuclear solution, and testing to obtain the nuclear with the particle size of 1.8 mu m. The glass transition temperature of the test core was 107 ℃.

2) Preparing a core-shell structure binder:

adding 112g of isooctyl acrylate, 208g of methyl methacrylate and 9.6g of trimethylolpropane triacrylate into the core solution in calculated amount, stirring for 3 hours, adding 10g of dibenzoyl peroxide, heating to 80 ℃, and reacting for 8 hours at 80 ℃ to obtain the white adhesive with the core-shell structure, wherein the mass ratio of the core to the shell is 1:1.68, the particle size of the test binder was 2.5 μm. The glass transition temperature of the shell was measured to be 30 ℃ by DSC.

Example 3

1) Preparation of the core solution:

adding 900g of water and 20g of PEG-2000 into a glass reaction kettle, uniformly stirring, adding 300g of styrene, 15g of divinylbenzene and 30g of butyl acrylate, stirring, introducing nitrogen for 30min, adding 5g of dimethyl azodiisobutyrate, heating to 78 ℃, reacting for 8h at 78 ℃, cooling to room temperature after the reaction is finished, obtaining a nuclear solution, and testing to obtain the nuclear with the particle size of 4.0 mu m. The glass transition temperature of the test core was 84 ℃.

2) Preparing a core-shell structure binder:

adding 64g of butyl acrylate, 256g of acrylonitrile and 5g of N- (hydroxymethyl) acrylamide into the core solution, stirring for 3 hours, adding 5g of dimethyl azodiisobutyrate, heating to 80 ℃, and reacting for 8 hours at 80 ℃ to obtain a white binder with a core-shell structure, wherein the mass ratio of the core to the shell is 1:0.95, the particle size of the test binder was 5.0. Mu.m. The glass transition temperature of the shell was measured to be 70 ℃ using DSC.

The glass transition temperature of the shell was measured by DSC to be 40 ℃.
